title: Runloop pocket journal — Doria (oncall notes + follow-ups)
body:
Quick pocket-journal for the middle of runloop; keep terse. Purpose: capture pages, follow-ups, and immediate runbook TODOs I need to own or hand off. Not exhaustive.

2026-06-18 01:12 — page from paging service: high 5xx rate on hosted-api-prod us-west-2
- Pager: alerts spike from 01:10–01:16, ~180 reqs/min with 11% 5xx. Downstream error class: 'kv-cache-miss' then cascade NPE in serving runtime.
- Action taken: rolled back model-variant->v2-alpha to v2-stable on route /generate (canary policy). Traffic dropped 5xx to baseline within 2 mins. Left canary disabled.
- Notes: rollback via console worked but UI showed stale capacity numbers for ~30s. Confirmed autoscaler metrics still correct.

2026-06-18 01:40 — short post-incident checklist
- Create quick incident summary (for CS) — Doria to draft short note.
- Tag traces: add trace ids to incident ticket SRE-1427 (Mateo to attach full spans).
- Who to ping: infra-kernel team for potential KV cache root cause; assigned to Zoe.

Immediate runbook TODOs (scratch items)
- [ ] Add step to runtime rollback playbook: verify console capacity widget vs API (cmd: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RW_TOKEN' https://api.redwood.internal/v1/capacity/… )
- [ ] Add explicit telemetry for 'kv-cache-miss' counters exposed to datadog (metric name suggestion: serving.runtime.kv_cache.misses) — request via infra-metrics ticket.
- [x] Update canary policy docs to include fallback thresholds (done 02:20)

Notes to self: what looked weird
- cascade begins with repeated small KV timeouts (~120–180ms) — increased concurrency caused NPE where handler expected non-null cached pointer. Suspect race after quantization cache invalidation.
- Check PRs merged in last 24h for cache invalidation code: PR #838 flagged in linked_artifacts.

Commands / queries I ran (for my notes)
- kubectl -n rw-serving logs -l app=serving-runtime --since=30m | grep 'kv-cache' | tail -n 200
- curl -s 'https://api.redwood.internal/v1/health/kv?region=us-west-2' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RW_TOKEN' | jq .latency_summary
- datadog query metric: avg:serving.runtime.kv_cache.duration{env:prod}.rollup(avg, 60)

Follow-ups assigned / owners
- Zoe: open infra bug for cache race, include heap/profile from host rw-kv-04 (ZOOM on Mon 10:30).
- Mateo: attach span traces and heatmap to SRE-1427, link to CS summary (ETA today EOD).
- Doria (me): draft customer-facing blurb for impacted customers, include rollback details + mitigation steps.

Postmortem thinking (high level)
- Blame: not a single person; combination of recent cache invalidation refactor + increased request concurrency after marketing campaign + insufficient guardrails in canary fallback thresholds.
- Primary mitigation candidates: revert refactor to stable behavior OR harden cache invalidation with lockless check; add circuit-breaker on kv timeouts; tighten canary thresholds and automatic rollback (shorter window).

SRE runbook edits (things to add)
- explicit sanity check: if kv-cache miss rate > 2% AND avg latency > 80ms for > 2 min then set route policy to route->stable.
- include documented command to force-disable canary via API (not just console).
- add 'who to call' list for infra-kernel and runtime teams with rotation.

Fragile ideas / hypotheses to test
- hypothesis A: garbage collector pauses combined with lock acquisition order caused null deref during cache repopulate under burst. Test by reproducing under load with heap-profiling.
- hypothesis B: quantization warming path triggers cache eviction in new refactor; check eviction logs and cache TTLs.

Small personal TODOs (today)
- [ ] finish CS blurb and send to Mateo for approval (priority: high)
- [ ] update runbook draft with the three explicit checks above
- [ ] create infra-metrics ticket for kv_cache.misses metric and link SRE-1427
- [ ] drop a note in #sre-runloop summarizing immediate actions and owners

Loose notes for handover to next oncall (to copy into handoff doc)
- most recent action: canary disabled, route pinned to stable model variant. Autoscaler still green.
- open items: infra bug (Zoe), traces (Mateo), CS blurb (Doria). Anything not closed by 12:00 UTC tomorrow escalate to oncall lead.

Random crumbs / one-off reminders
- check if customer X received degraded latency alerts (ticket CX-912)
- ask product about traffic ramp schedule tomorrow 08:00 US/PST (might coincide with planned batch jobs)

End notes: keep this doc ephemeral. Will move cleaned tasks to SRE tickets and handoff doc. If nothing else, copy the TODO checklist into the official handoff before end-of-shift.
